case.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
case.limits: The filter caused harm without any third-party content doing the work. Where the injury runs through generated words rather than a feature's mechanics, courts still have to decide whether the design frame or the speech frame controls.
case.holding: Section 230 did not bar a negligent-design claim against Snapchat for its speed filter, because the claim faulted the design of the product itself rather than treating Snap as the publisher of any user's content.
case.why_ai_cites_it: The road around Zeran. Plaintiffs suing AI companies over harmful system behaviour plead design defect precisely because Lemmon holds that a duty to design reasonably exists independent of publishing, which is why current chatbot cases are framed as defective products rather than harmful speech.
